age.evidence: Adult male and female WT and βArr1-KO, and WT and βArr2-KO mice were used in these experiments

sex.evidence: Adult male and female WT and βArr1-KO, and WT and βArr2-KO mice were used in these experiments. No sex effects were detected in any experiments.

dosing.evidence: The vehicle was composed of N,N-dimethyllacetamide (final volume 0.5%) that was brought to volume with 5% 2-hydroxypropoyl-β-cyclodextrin in water. All drugs were administered (i.p.) in a 5 mL/kg volume.

handling.evidence: Methods do not mention any handling protocol.

day_night_flipped.evidence: on a 14:10 h (lights on at 0600 h) light-dark cycle

assays.assay_description: Open field (21 × 21 × 30 cm, 180 lux). 30 min baseline, then injection of vehicle or 0.3 mg/kg LSD (with/without MDL100907 pretreatment) and 90 min recording. Beam-break measures: distance traveled, rearing, stereotypical activities, recorded in 5-min blocks.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered (i.p.) in a 5 mL/kg volume

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were injected with vehicle or MDL and placed into the open field. Thirty min later, they were administered LSD and immediately returned to the open field for 90 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals moved freely in the open field arena.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in open field apparatus during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in open field apparatus during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: administered the vehicle or LSD and were immediately returned to the open field for 90 min

outcomes.summary: LSD (0.3 mg/kg) increased locomotor activity in WT and βArr1-KO mice; rearing and stereotypy were also stimulated in βArr2-WT mice. βArr2-KO mice showed blunted/absent responses. MDL100907 (0.1 and 0.5 mg/kg) blocked LSD-stimulated motor activity.
outcomes.statistics: Locomotion βArr1: F(4,93)=16.916, p<0.001. Locomotion βArr2: F(5,96)=18.578, p<0.001, genotype×treatment F(5,96)=5.273, p<0.001. Rearing βArr2: F(5,96)=7.150, p<0.001. Stereotypy βArr2: F(5,96)=4.242, p=0.002.
outcomes.evidence: LSD stimulates motor activities to similar extents in WT and βArr1-KO animals... LSD was more potent in stimulating cumulative locomotor activities in the WT than in the βArr2-KO mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: locomotor activity (distance traveled), rearing (vertical beam-breaks), and stereotypical activities (repetitive beam-breaks less than 1 s)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Motor activity was monitored... in 5-min blocks or as cumulative activities (Supplementary Figures S1-S2 show 5-min interval time-course)

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No sequence/transition analysis for locomotor measures.

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotion, rearing and stereotypy beam-breaks are not ethological behaviours.

B5_social.evidence: Animals tested individually; no social construct.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Motor activity was monitored using Fusion Versamax 5.3 Edition software (beam-break system)

E2_shelter.evidence: Open field arena with no shelter.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding in open field apparatus.

E6_spatial.evidence: Standard open field is a single arena.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in apparatus.

D1_continuity.evidence: Single open field session per mouse (baseline + post-injection continuous).

D2_session_duration.evidence: 30 min baseline + 90 min post-injection = 120 min continuous recording

D3_recording_days.evidence: All open-field data collected on a single day.

D4_baseline.evidence: The cumulative baseline motor activities (0-30 min) are presented in Supplementary Table S1

assays.assay_name: Head Twitch, Grooming, and Retrograde Walking (video-scored in open field)
assays.assay_description: First 30 min after LSD injection in the open field were video-recorded. Blinded observers scored number of head twitches, duration of grooming (including organization/sequence of grooming bouts), and incidences of retrograde walking.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice had 30 min in open field before LSD injection (same apparatus exposure prior to recording window for these behaviors).

food_restriction.evidence: No food in apparatus during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in apparatus during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: scored over the first 30 min following injection of the vehicle or LSD

sample_size.evidence: N = 8-17 mice/group for head twitch, grooming, and retrograde walking

outcomes.summary: LSD robustly increased head twitches, grooming duration, and incidences of retrograde walking in WT and βArr1-KO mice. Grooming sequence was disrupted (abbreviated/non-sequential) in WT and βArr1-KO but largely intact in βArr2-KO. βArr2-KO mice had severely blunted or absent responses. MDL100907 blocked all LSD effects.
outcomes.statistics: HTR βArr1: F(4,93)=114.447, p<0.001. Grooming βArr1: F(4,93)=61.232, p<0.001. Retrograde walking βArr1: F(4,93)=43.899, p<0.001. HTR βArr2: genotype F(1,96)=31.271, p<0.001; treatment F(5,96)=41.567, p<0.001; interaction F(5,96)=7.734, p<0.001. Grooming βArr2: genotype F(1,96)=51.972, p<0.001. Retrograde walking βArr2: F(5,96)=13.028, p<0.001.
outcomes.evidence: LSD robustly stimulates many surrogates of psychedelic drug actions including head twitches, grooming, retrograde walking... in WT and βArr1-KO animals. By contrast, in βArr2-KO mice head twitch responses are low with LSD and this psychedelic is without effects on other surrogates.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Head twitches, grooming duration, grooming sequence organization, and retrograde walking incidences were measured.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Responses summed over the first 30 min, no within-session time-course.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: Analyses of the videorecordings confirmed that all genotypes engaged in a normal sequence of grooming beginning with the face, progressing down the body, and ending at the feet or tail... When LSD was administered, the sequence of grooming became abbreviated, non-sequential

B4_ethological.evidence: Grooming and retrograde walking are natural rodent ethological behaviours scored as distinct acts.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Observers who were blinded... scored the video recordings (manual scoring).

D2_session_duration.evidence: scored over the first 30 min following injection

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline 30 min was for locomotor beam-break measures; HTR/grooming/retrograde were scored only post-injection.

assays.assay_name: Nose-Poking in 5-Choice Serial Reaction Time Apparatus
assays.assay_description: 5-choice serial reaction-time chamber (Med Associates) with five infrared-detected nose-poke apertures, no reward. Mice injected with vehicle or MDL, returned to home cage; 30 min later injected with vehicle or LSD and placed into chamber for 30 min. Number of nose pokes recorded.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice injected and returned to home-cage, then placed immediately into the operant chambers; no prior apparatus habituation described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice freely moving in operant chamber.

food_restriction.evidence: No food or liquid reward was available

water_restriction.evidence: No food or liquid reward was available

time_to_assay.evidence: the animals were injected with the vehicle or LSD and were placed immediately into the operant chambers for 30 min

outcomes.summary: LSD (0.3 mg/kg) increased nose-poking in WT and βArr1-KO mice but had no effect in βArr2-KO mice. All doses of MDL100907 reduced LSD-stimulated nose poking to control levels.
outcomes.evidence: LSD stimulated nose-poking behaviors relative to all other groups (p < 0.007)... No treatment effects were noted among the βArr2-KO animals.

B1_num_measures.evidence: The data are depicted as the numbers of head pokes

B4_ethological.evidence: Nose poking into operant apertures is not a natural ethological behavior.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: infrared diodes to register nose pokes (Med Associates beam-break system)

E6_spatial.evidence: Five apertures arranged within a single operant chamber (no walled compartments).

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or liquid reward was available

D2_session_duration.evidence: placed immediately into the operant chambers for 30 min

assays.assay_description: PPI in SR-LAB chambers. Mice pretreated with vehicle/MDL100907/haloperidol, then 15 min later injected with vehicle or 0.3 mg/kg LSD and placed in chamber. After 10 min habituation to 64 dB white noise, 42 trials (null, 120 dB pulse-alone, prepulse-pulse at 4/8/12 dB above background) were delivered. %PPI calculated.

setup_habituation.evidence: After 10 min of habituation to a white noise background (64 dB), testing began

setup_restrain.evidence: PPI of the acoustic startle response was conducted using SR-LAB chambers (animals placed in startle holders).

time_to_assay.evidence: Fifteen min later the animals received the vehicle or LSD and were placed into the apparatus. After 10 min of habituation... testing began

outcomes.summary: LSD (0.3 mg/kg) disrupted PPI in WT and βArr1-KO mice but not in βArr2-KO mice. MDL100907 restored PPI in WT mice from both strains; haloperidol was required to restore PPI in βArr1-KO mice.
outcomes.statistics: βArr1 PPI: prepulse F(1,91)=487.507, p<0.001; genotype F(1,91)=25.358, p<0.001; treatment F(4,91)=11.435, p<0.001. Haloperidol study: treatment F(3,72)=9.591, p<0.001. βArr2 PPI: genotype F(1,74)=18.823, p<0.001; treatment F(4,74)=3.953, p=0.006; genotype×treatment F(4,74)=5.660, p<0.001.
outcomes.evidence: LSD disrupted PPI in both βArr1 genotypes relative to their vehicle and 0.5 mg/kg MDL controls (p values ≤ 0.002)... PPI in βArr2-KO mice was unaffected by LSD.

B1_num_measures.evidence: %PPI, startle (120 dB) response, and null activity all reported.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single overall %PPI per trial type, no within-session time-course.

B4_ethological.evidence: PPI startle magnitude is not an ethological behaviour.

B6_cognitive.evidence: PPI is sensorimotor gating, not learning/memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Force-transducer startle measure; no video-based behaviour classifier.

D2_session_duration.evidence: 10 min habituation + 42 trials; total session ≥15 min.

judge_notes: Merged candidate qwen's single combined 'Open Field' assay (which included HTR/grooming/retrograde) with glm's per-behavior split: kept locomotor beam-break measures as one assay (Open Field locomotion/rearing/stereotypy) and the manually video-scored ethological behaviors (HTR, grooming, retrograde walking) as a second assay since they share apparatus but use a different measurement modality (manual video scoring of distinct acts) and a different scoring window (first 30 min post-injection only).

Did not split HTR, grooming, and retrograde walking into separate assays because they were all scored from the same video recording over the same 30-min window using identical methodology — treated as one ethological-scoring assay with multiple measures.

B1 for Open Field locomotion set to 4-6 to include locomotion, rearing, stereotypy (3 base measures) plus the analyses incorporate cumulative and time-course views; conservative score of 2 (4-6) accepted as in qwen.
Set PPI setup_restrain = yes per rubric (SR-LAB tubes count as body restraint) — overriding gptoss's 'not_reported' and qwen's 'yes'.
Excluded radioligand binding and immunohistochemistry sections — ex vivo molecular work, not behavioural assays.
DOI left null — paper masthead not in Docling output and candidates disagreed (one fabricated a DOI).
Vehicle classified as 'cyclodextrin' (2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin is the bulk solvent; DMA is co-solvent at 0.5%).
